findings.explanation: The paper root connects manuscript, analysis, image archive and three pinned components. Analysis input paths stay beneath that root. The upstream acquisition-only link does not establish that the delivered BIDS inputs used by this paper lie outside its logical boundary.

The discovery chain reaches the paper inputs through root gitlinks and the REMoDNaV evaluation-data gitlink. Content retrieval is deliberately untested. The machine-local acquisition-source URL is real, but the analysis reads delivered BIDS files rather than that acquisition repository; it is not an observed failure to retrieve required paper inputs.

The Docker recipe includes scientific and manuscript software, while REMoDNaV is an identified project component. Host orchestration tools have installation pointers. This supports inclusion under the method's equivalent-evidence rule, without implying that an unpinned rebuild recreates identical bytes.

Git trees and retained history identify the analysis, text, configuration and module revisions. Capture omissions do not represent an originally dirty tree. The assessment correctly questions the clean-tree probe as a measurement of version-control adoption.

The inspected tree contains six annex-pointer blobs, including approximately 78 MB and 1.75 GB image layers. StudyForrest also separates Git metadata from annex-managed data. Missing bytes do not undermine the observed content-versioning mechanism.

The main run records exit status, inputs, image directory and outputs, but declaring img does not demonstrate execution of quality_stats(). The figure is still used in the manuscript, and its last change has no environment-linked run. The label-generation record also lacks an environment reference. Partial is warranted.

Installation and usage instructions exist, but the README promises all figures while the invoked command omits quality_stats(), which produces velhist.svg. This is an actual documentation/mechanism conflict, not the accurately disclosed switch from the old virtualenv route.

The tagged rerun is an identifiable start and the Make target dispatches the principal computations. The active manuscript nevertheless retains velhist, whose generating function is not dispatched. The method requires at most partial for this incomplete documented route.

The root workflow uses relative object paths; container-internal paths are not host leaks. Following root .gitmodules to the label component reveals submit generators with a specific user directory and Python 2.7 executable. Partial is justified for the explicitly linked component scope, without claiming those generators run during the current paper rerun.

Imports on the supported paper route map to the declared scientific packages, including sklearn/scikit-learn and statsmodels. The image includes the manuscript commands, and the script tolerates absent in-image DataLad because inputs are provisioned by host orchestration. This is a source-level completeness judgment, not an installation result.

The README documents platforms and Docker compatibility. The configured adapter directly invokes Docker as the calling user and explicitly notes that this usable non-root Docker assumption needs documentation; the root instructions do not spell it out. Partial is defensible as a documentation gap, not evidence of a permission failure.
findings.suggested_correction: Keep the finding about a missing explicit host prerequisite; do not imply that Docker permissions were tested or that the externally linked installation guides were inspected in this frozen cohort.

findings.explanation: The updated requirements section identifies the orchestration tools and tested versions, and the Docker recipe enumerates the system and scientific packages. A clear dependency list exists despite the narrower host-configuration caveat under must/011.

Recipe, registration and archive metadata are tracked in the same immutable object as the code and module pins. The frozen tree directly supports this positive independently of whether archive payloads can currently be downloaded.

History supplies an executable image-build procedure, a later Dockerfile correction and completed build/save and conversion records. This exceeds a newly introduced specification with no subsequent maintenance instance. The duplicate flag is present and should/008 uses the same evidence.

The archived config and layer identities provide an exact reuse target. Historical tree inspection identifies the same f881bd4d config filename before OCI conversion, and the adapter hashes the config and runs its image ID. A local RepoTags value ending in latest does not make this a floating registry execution. Adapter discovery is README version reference to the configured adapter.

The frozen metadata provides source and content-location claims, not independent recipient retrieval of the image. Not-checked correctly preserves that distinction. The supplied metadata contains current docker-blobs locations as well as older docker-layers locations; neither is an observed successful download.
findings.suggested_correction: For citation precision, identify the current docker-blobs metadata alongside the older docker-layers entries, without changing not-checked.

findings.explanation: Environment acquisition and invocation are explained, but the native method explicitly groups must/017 with the A.1 documented-route checks and caps it at partial when documentation conflicts with the mechanism. The same README promise to recompute every figure contradicted by the uncalled quality_stats() was used to downgrade must/007 and must/008. Keeping must/017 met applies that rule inconsistently.
findings.suggested_correction: Change must/017 to partial. Preserve credit for the concrete environment instructions while identifying the all-figures coverage conflict. Do not penalize the explicitly disclosed old/new environment routes themselves.

findings.explanation: The discovered components are Git repositories with pinned gitlinks; git-annex/DataLad extend that same tracking model for large content. No conflicting component-versioning mechanism was identified in the inspected route.

The retained completed maintenance runs are stronger evidence than a CI filename, while library Travis configuration is not proof of paper-workflow execution. The explicit all-figure instruction mismatch gives a concrete reason for partial; two episodic records alone do not establish continuing regular verification.

Raw gaze, derived labels and algorithm are separate linked components. Analysis source, generated statistics/figures and environment are distinguishable paths. The method does not require every such path to be an independent repository, so the positive is supported.

The historical record is a completed analysis execution, not merely a script definition. Its configured Docker adapter launches a new container and removes it. This meets the method's allowance for equivalent historical completed-run evidence; it does not certify every manuscript result or constitute a fresh run by this reviewer.

Each adapter invocation executes docker run with --rm, and registration gives the process a temporary HOME. Persistent mounted outputs and a reused image do not imply reuse of the execution container. This supports the stated disposable-environment design.

The image was exercised in a completed analysis and later a successful load/exit/conversion action. These are real but limited reconstitution checks, with no retained recurring full validation procedure. Partial appropriately credits those checks rather than equating absence of root CI with complete absence of testing.

The object records an actual saved image with identified layers, plus completed build/save and later conversion actions. That is archival evidence beyond a registry name. Inspection cannot verify the withheld image contents or present-day retrieval, which the assessment correctly handles separately.

The executable maintenance actions and tracked subsequent changes support the same positive as must/014. Both responses mark the upstream duplicate, so this is consistent repeated coverage of one question, not two independent maintenance practices.

The consumed data advertises unrestricted access and the algorithm has a public software license. No access-controlled component is identified on the analysis route. A historical local path alone does not demonstrate restricted access, so the empty-subject N/A interpretation is supported without claiming that public payload retrieval was verified.

Independent datasets and algorithm components are explicitly linked. Recursively following raw_eyegaze exposes an acquisition repository linked by a machine-local URL; that is a genuine incomplete module-link boundary even though it is not required to consume the delivered paper inputs. The assessment correctly avoids treating ordinary Python packages as missing project modules.

Module discovery reaches a label README whose reproduction account still names removed preprocessing/detection scripts, while retained execution evidence uses compute_all.sh and the linked REMoDNaV package. That mismatch impairs understanding of how raw inputs, algorithm and derived labels relate and can be recombined, supporting partial.

Separate repository pins and focused label/algorithm pointer updates establish independent component boundaries. The assessment properly qualifies that this is structural update capability, not a promise that arbitrary future algorithm revisions preserve results.

Gitlinks define assembly of component revisions, and the container registration plus run input/output declarations connect them into the paper computation. This directly supports a composition mechanism without requiring proof of a newly executed workflow.

The cited defect concerns obsolete reproduction commands, but this criterion asks for documentation or tooling supporting navigation and understanding of modular structure. The assessment itself credits .gitmodules/DataLad navigation, and the current module names and paths resolve structurally. It does not explain what navigation capability is missing despite that alternative tooling route.
findings.suggested_correction: Reconsider met for the available module-navigation tooling, or identify a concrete structural-navigation failure that makes the tooling/documentation only partially adequate. Retain the obsolete reproduction instructions under the actionable and relationship/recombination findings rather than automatically reusing them here.

limitations: Inspection-only review of the assigned anonymized native assessment and the source boundary frozen by data/remodnav-evidence.json#sha256=e3c6253bced7d959cd59873c3d49d166bf5793906bcdf65e49e265076d215499. No other assessments, peer reviews, examples, gold answers, methods or object caches were read.

No network calls, scientific execution, container builds, payload acquisition or fresh rerun occurred. All Git reads set GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1. Binary/annex data and container layers are absent by design; their absence is not evidence of failed retrieval.

Checked the manifest hash, all 260 supplied source-file hashes, seven history hashes and nine external/availability metadata hashes. Following root documentation, explicit module links and run history established the relevant discovery paths; cache presence alone was not treated as discoverability.

Native checklist pin validation and assessment validation passed. Independently inspected the material source citations and historical run records; validation success was not used as support for judgments. All 31 native criterion IDs are present, with denominators 17 MUST, 9 SHOULD and 5 MAY. The assigned JSON contains no aggregate numeric score or report denominator to audit. Its two not-checked items and one not-applicable item remain distinct from failures.

The separate original probe receipt and human report were not supplied as authorized review inputs. Probe-output assertions can therefore be checked against source properties but not fully authenticated as original probe receipts.

Historical completed-run metadata supports execution claims but does not establish current numerical repeatability or scientific validity. Remote issue discussions and external installation guides were not available in the frozen package. The Docker adapter is a supplied versioned external source reached from the README tool/version reference and configured invocation, not a bundled project file; its exact frozen bytes are cited by SHA256.
Actual observed runtime model identity is unavailable and is recorded as null. Agreement with individual criteria is independent technical review, not human approval.
